title: Mardonios comes down to the sea
prose: In the spring of 492 Darius removes every other commander and gives the war to one man: Mardonios, son of Gobryas, young, and lately married to the king's daughter. He brings a very large land-army and a very large naval force down to Kilikia, puts the army on the road, and boards a ship himself.

title: Thasos, and then the mountain
prose: Thasos is taken without a hand raised in its defence. Macedonia is made to serve. Then the fleet crosses from Thasos and works along the coast to Acanthos, and tries to get round Mount Athos — and a violent north wind falls on it. THREE HUNDRED SHIPS AND MORE THAN TWENTY THOUSAND MEN. Herodotus itemises how they died: taken by the sea monsters that fill that water, dashed on the rocks, drowned not knowing how to swim, dead of the cold. He reports it as `it is said`, and the monsters arrive in the same breath as the arithmetic.

title: And the army fares no better
prose: While the fleet is dying at Athos, the land-army is camped in Macedonia and is attacked in the night by the Brygian Thracians. Many are killed and Mardonios himself is wounded. He will not leave until he has subdued them, and then leads the army home having lost heavily by both land and sea. THE FIRST EXPEDITION ENDS WITHOUT REACHING GREECE.

title: Remember the Athenians
prose: Two years pass and the design does not. Darius is put in mind of the Athenians continually by his servant; the sons of Peisistratos are at his court, bringing charges; and there is the pretext he wanted — the cities that would not give earth and water. He takes the command from Mardonios, who had failed, and gives it to Datis and Artaphrenes.

title: A fleet built for horses, and a route chosen out of fear
prose: They muster on the Aleian plain in Kilikia, and the whole naval armament comes up to them — SIX HUNDRED TRIREMES, and with them the ships for carrying horses, WHICH DARIUS HAD ORDERED HIS TRIBUTARIES TO BUILD THE YEAR BEFORE. The horses go aboard, the army goes aboard, and they sail for Ionia. Then they do not coast the mainland. They cross from Samos by the Icarian Sea and go island to island — because, Herodotus thinks, they feared above all else the voyage round Athos. THE WRECK IS STILL DECIDING THE ROUTE TWO YEARS LATER.

title: Naxos first, remembering the former events
prose: Naxos is the first island and it is chosen on purpose — they came against it first, remembering what had happened there before. The Naxians do not wait: they leave for the mountains. Those caught are made slaves, and the temples and the town are burned. Then the fleet puts out to sea for the other islands. NAXOS IS OUTSIDE THIS FRAME and cannot be drawn on it; the next chapter is Delos, and the map begins there.
